description: sensitive_elements_present: false and confidential_elements_present: false sit uneasily with regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted, HIPAA-oriented handling, static watermarking of released copies, verified-ID access gating and an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk. A release that genuinely contains nothing sensitive or confidential would not normally require that control stack; the two blocks appear to answer the healthsheet's narrow questions rather than characterise the release as governed.
recommendation: Qualify sensitive_elements/confidential_elements to state that the released variables are not themselves sensitive while the release remains access-controlled because of residual re-identification risk, so the two claims are read together rather than as a contradiction.

description: is_deidentified carries three mutually inconsistent source statements: FAIRhub records 'NoDeIdentification' (no identifiers collected), the RO-Crate records the release as deidentified, and the Nature Metabolism comment describes HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping. The structured method field asserts the strongest of the three (HIPAA Safe Harbor) while deidentification_details reports all three unreconciled.
recommendation: State which statement the project treats as authoritative for the released files, or record the method as 'Safe Harbor verification, no identifiers collected' so the structured value and the prose do not diverge.

description: No download_url field is populated. The download route is nevertheless reconstructable from page, data_governance.access_review_process (verified-ID login, T2DM-only attestation, license assent) and the external resource https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access, so the sub-element's purpose is met by platform access instructions rather than by a direct link.
recommendation: Populate download_url with https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 or the access endpoint so machine clients can resolve the retrieval route without parsing prose.

description: distribution_formats lists DICOM, CSV, JSON and Markdown, but the release also distributes WFDB electrocardiography records, Open mHealth wearable/CGM payloads and NASA ESDS-style ASCII environmental files per conforms_to and file_collections. The distribution list is narrower than the standards list, and no character encoding is stated anywhere.
recommendation: Add distribution_formats entries for WFDB and the Open mHealth/ESDS text payloads with their media types, and record character encoding (e.g. UTF-8) for the text-based collections.

description: is_tabular: false while the description states the modalities 'encompass tabular data, imaging data and physiological signal/waveform data' and clinical_data is distributed as one-to-one OMOP CDM CSV tables. The flag is defensible for a multimodal release that is not a single table, but read alone it contradicts the description.
recommendation: Note beside is_tabular that the release is multimodal and that tabular content is confined to the OMOP clinical_data collection and participants.tsv.

description: No software that produced or transformed the released data is named. Conversion of Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt exports to DICOM, of Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, and mapping of clinical data to OMOP CDM are described as having happened, but no tool, package, version or repository is attached to any of those steps, and no used_software is recorded on preprocessing_strategies or cleaning_strategies. The software that is named occupies non-qualifying roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture instrumentation; FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure is hosting; the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation of the released data; https://github.com/AI-READI is an organisation root that identifies the publisher rather than a piece of software.
recommendation: Name the converters and mapping pipelines (tool name, version, and the AI-READI repository that holds each) on preprocessing_strategies.used_software so a reader can tell what produced the distributed DICOM, OMOP and Open mHealth files.

description: variables provides 20 measures with name, data type, unit, description and measurement technique, but no ontology or concept identifiers (LOINC, OMOP concept_id, SNOMED) are attached, and source_caveats records that the authoritative per-domain data dictionary at docs.aireadi.org was not consulted. Variable coverage is therefore illustrative rather than exhaustive for a 356,343-file multimodal release.
recommendation: Attach concept identifiers to each variable and link the released participants.json / per-domain data dictionary as the authoritative variable reference.

description: No errata block and no data_protection_impacts (DPIA) block. Change information is instead carried by updates.update_details and version_access.version_details, and data-protection reasoning by participant_privacy and ethical_reviews, so both sub-elements are satisfied through their alternative fields rather than left undocumented.
recommendation: Add an errata list (empty with a statement if none are known) and a short DPIA record referencing the re-identification analysis already present in future_use_impacts.

description: Institutional attribution is internally contradictory across the record: Washington University in St. Louis is named as licensor, accountable organization and PI affiliation, while the reviewing IRB, the award recipient per NIH RePORTER and the assay laboratory are all University of Washington. The record discloses the conflict in source_caveats rather than resolving it, which is honest but leaves accountable_organization pointing at an institution that no human-subjects or award evidence supports.
recommendation: Resolve the attribution with the project, or mark accountable_organization as reported-by-FAIRhub and name the University of Washington as the human-subjects and award institution.

description: Collection start is given as 2023-07-19 in collection_timeframes and the description while the BMJ Open protocol states 18 July 2023; license naming differs between two tier-1 sources ('AI-READI custom license v2.0' in the API, 'Health Data License' on the dataset page); a healthsheet answer describing first-year coverage contradicts the stated 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window. All three are disclosed and adjudicated by source tier rather than left silent.
recommendation: Retain the tier adjudication; where the project can confirm a single value upstream, cite the confirmation so downstream consumers stop inheriting the ambiguity.

description: No software that produced or transformed the distributed data is named. preprocessing_strategies states that Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt exports were 'converted to DICOM', Garmin .FIT 'converted to the Open mHealth standard', ECG 'converted to WFDB', and that clinical data were 'mapped to' the OMOP CDM, but no converter, mapper or pipeline is identified; processing is described only as 'a combination of automated and custom processing'. The named software in the record occupies non-qualifying roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture, FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure is hosting, the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation, and https://github.com/AI-READI is an organization root that identifies the publisher rather than a tool.
recommendation: Name the conversion and OMOP-mapping software with versions and repository or DOI links (for example the specific .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM converters and the FIT-to-Open-mHealth tooling), attaching them via used_software on preprocessing_strategies.

description: No download_url slot is populated even though the release is publicly downloadable. Access is nevertheless actionable from other slots: distribution_formats.access_urls gives https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access and data_governance.access_review_process records the FAIRhub access type 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' and the three steps required.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the FAIRhub download endpoint so that machine agents need not infer it from distribution_formats.

description: The de-identification evidence carries an internal tension the record itself surfaces: is_deidentified.deidentification_details reports the FAIRhub deIdentType as 'NoDeIdentification' with deIdentHIPAA true, while is_deidentified.method asserts the public set is stripped of PHI 'via the Safe Harbor method'. The record reconciles this by explaining that no identifiers were collected so no active de-identification step was necessary, which is a coherent reading, but the two statements read as contradictory in isolation.
recommendation: State explicitly that 'NoDeIdentification' denotes the absence of a removal step on an already identifier-free collection, rather than the absence of HIPAA conformance.

description: total_size_bytes is stated as 3,815,969,779,678 while the nine file_collections directory sizes sum to 3,815,969,360,064, a difference of 419,614 bytes that no source accounts for. The record discloses this discrepancy in source_caveats and attributes it plausibly to the root-level metadata files.
recommendation: Publish a byte count for the root metadata directory so that the stated total reconciles with the per-directory sums.

description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted' and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' are the record's own mappings onto the schema vocabulary, not values any source states; the only source value is the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)'. The record declares this inference in source_caveats rather than presenting the enum values as sourced, which is the correct handling, but a consumer reading only the structured slot would not see the inference.
recommendation: Carry the source value 'HL7:2N (normal)' in a notes field adjacent to the enum so the mapping is visible at the point of use.

description: variables documents 13 variables (participant_id, seven laboratory analytes, MoCA, visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, CGM, particulate matter) for a release whose clinical_data directory is a one-to-one mapping of OMOP CDM tables covering surveys, assessments and laboratory results. Variable-level coverage is therefore illustrative rather than exhaustive, though the entries present carry data_type, unit, measurement_technique, reference ranges and an is_identifier flag.
recommendation: Reference participants.json and the OMOP CDM table definitions as the authoritative data dictionary, or state explicitly that the variables list is a curated subset.

description: data_governance records committee_name, accountable_organization, access_review_process and stewardship_roles but no committee_contact. A contact is reachable elsewhere (maintainers gives contact@aireadi.org and https://aireadi.org/contact; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board gives hsdrely@uw.edu for the IRB Reliance Team), so the governance-contact requirement is met in substance but not in the dedicated slot.
recommendation: Populate data_governance.committee_contact with the Data Access Committee or consortium governance contact.

description: Three named evidence slots are empty where their subject matter is nevertheless addressed in prose: errata (change information is instead in updates.update_details and version_access.version_details), imputation_protocols (missing-value handling is in missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy), and data_protection_impacts (the notes field states that no data protection impact analysis has been conducted).
recommendation: Populate the dedicated slots, including an explicit negative for data_protection_impacts, so the negative findings currently buried in notes become machine-readable.

description: Element 8 sub-element 4: the record describes format conversion and processing of the released data (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, 'a combination of automated and custom processing') but never names the software that performed any of it. Every piece of software named in the record occupies an excluded role: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture and data-entry tools (role a); FAIRhub is the hosting and dissemination platform (role b); the RO-Crate packaging wraps the release without transforming its contents (role c); the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard, supported by the included dqd_omop.json, is a validation aid for downstream users (role d). The GitHub pointer is an organization root (https://github.com/AI-READI) that identifies the publisher rather than a named conversion or processing tool.
recommendation: Name the conversion and processing software with versions (for example the .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM converters, the Garmin .FIT-to-mHealth converter and the OMOP ETL tooling) and link the specific repositories under the AI-READI GitHub organization rather than the organization root.

description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is set to 'restricted', a value the record itself states is its own substitution that 'does not reproduce, and on its face contradicts' the only sourced classification, the RO-Crate's HL7:2N (normal). It also sits against confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: false. The substitution is disclosed rather than concealed, which is good practice, but the asserted enum value is not supported by any source.
recommendation: Either carry the sourced HL7:2N value in a notes-bearing slot and leave the enum unset, or add an explicit crosswalk justifying the mapping from HL7:2N to 'restricted' on the basis of the access gating rather than the sensitivity classification.

description: Three incompatible characterizations of deidentification are carried simultaneously: is_deidentified.method reports FAIRhub's 'NoDeIdentification' with identifiable_elements_present: false (no identifiers collected into the release), the RO-Crate records deidentified: true, and the Nature Metabolism comment describes HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping of Protected Health Information. Safe Harbor stripping and 'no de-identification was necessary' are different operational claims about the same release. The record documents the disagreement in source_caveats rather than resolving it.
recommendation: State which operation was actually performed on the released files (a Safe Harbor review versus a confirmation that no identifiers were ever routed into the release) and demote the other characterizations to provenance notes.

description: sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present is true, enumerating EHR, wearable, ECG, environmental and CGM categories from the RO-Crate, while the FAIRhub healthsheet position recorded in the same block asserts the public dataset contains no sensitive data, and confidential_elements_present is false. Both tier-1 positions are retained without adjudication.
recommendation: Adjudicate on the released files specifically: the categories the RO-Crate lists are all present in the public release, which favours the affirmative flag with the healthsheet answer scoped to direct identifiers.

description: sampling_strategies.is_sample is false while the same block documents non-probability, wave-based stratified recruitment from an EHR-derived study base with deliberate under- and oversampling. The record scopes is_sample to enrollment completeness and warns the reader, but the boolean read alone contradicts the prose.
recommendation: Set is_sample true with respect to the target population and keep the enrollment-completeness claim in prose, or add an explicit scope qualifier to the boolean.

description: No download_url slot is populated. Access is nonetheless fully actionable: page gives https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and data_governance.access_review_process publishes the access route at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access together with the exact conditions (verified ID login, type-2-diabetes-research attestation, license acceptance, access type PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired).
recommendation: Populate download_url with the FAIRhub access endpoint so machine clients do not have to parse the governance prose.

description: No errata slot is populated. Change documentation is carried by updates.update_details pointing at the CHANGELOG, by the version_access note that 2.0.0 is no longer accessible, and by the known_limitations entry recording that Snellen visual acuity variables were dropped in 3.0.0; no corrections to previously released values are reported as such.
recommendation: Add an errata list, or state explicitly that no corrections to previously released data have been issued, so the silence is distinguishable from an omission.

description: instances.data_topic carries the bare CURIE B2AI_TOPIC:43 with no label or resolvable URI, so the coded topic is not machine- or human-resolvable from the record alone. The condition coverage is recoverable from description, subpopulations and known_limitations (type 2 diabetes across four severity arms), which is why the sub-element still passes.
recommendation: Add the human-readable label and a resolvable prefix expansion for the B2AI_TOPIC CURIE.

description: Unresolved institutional attribution: the acronym expansion ('Exploratory' versus 'Equitable'), the lead institution (Washington University in St. Louis as FAIRhub managing organization and license Licensor versus University of Washington as RO-Crate PI affiliation and NIH RePORTER awardee) and the publisher (FAIRhub versus AI-READI Consortium) each differ between equally ranked sources. The record carries both positions in source_caveats rather than asserting one silently, which is the correct handling, but a consumer of creators.principal_investigator.affiliation receives two affiliations for one person.
recommendation: Distinguish the roles explicitly: administering/sponsoring institution versus the PI's academic department, which would let both values stand without conflict.

description: The RO-Crate copyright notice quoted in ip_restrictions reads 'Copyright (c) 2026 AI-READI' for a release issued 2025-11-17. The value is faithfully quoted from the source, so this is a source artifact rather than a record error, but it is temporally inconsistent with issued and distribution_dates.
recommendation: Note the discrepancy against the source rather than leaving the future-dated notice unremarked.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=true (hospital records of critically ill patients, including PICU and NICU admissions) but no IRB, ethics committee of record, approval number, determination, or data protection impact assessment is documented. ethical_reviews describes project-level ethics activity (focus groups, legal landscape analysis) rather than review or oversight of this dataset, and its own source_caveats states that no IRB or determination is reported.
recommendation: Add the IRB or ethics committee of record with approval or determination identifiers (or an explicit statement of the reliance/waiver arrangement under which the multicenter retrospective extract is shared), and record a DPIA if one exists.

description: involves_human_subjects=true but informed_consent is entirely absent. For a retrospective multicenter clinical extract a consent waiver is plausible, but neither consent procedures nor a waiver determination are documented anywhere in the record.
recommendation: State the consent basis explicitly: written/verbal consent, broad consent for secondary use, or an IRB waiver of consent with the waiving authority.

description: is_deidentified.method describes techniques (tokenization, transformation limiting re-identification, imaging de-identification) but no identifiers-removed list and no named standard (HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) for the structured OMOP data; participant_privacy.reidentification_risk correspondingly reports no residual-risk assessment.
recommendation: Name the de-identification standard applied to structured data, enumerate identifier categories removed or generalized, and report the residual re-identification risk determination underpinning enclave-only access.

description: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included=true (minors and neonates via PICU/NICU admissions) but no protections, assent procedures, guardian permission or compensation arrangements are documented; participant_compensation is absent.
recommendation: Document the additional protections applied to pediatric and neonatal records (access conditions, small-cell suppression, guardian permission or waiver), or state affirmatively that none beyond the general controls apply.

description: Cohort size is reported inconsistently across sources and left unreconciled: description and instances record 50,000 admissions while source_caveats records the webinar figure of 'over 45K unique admissions'. Imaging is likewise counted in two incompatible units (7,642 admissions with radiology data versus 1,000 images available). The record discloses both discrepancies transparently but a reuser cannot determine the released cohort size.
recommendation: Pin the released counts to a dated release manifest and state the unit (admissions versus image series) for each modality.

description: No persistent identifier for the dataset: doi is absent and id is 'https://chorus4ai.org/', the project homepage, which is byte-identical to page. A homepage URL is neither dataset-specific nor persistence-guaranteed, so the dataset cannot be uniquely cited or resolved.
recommendation: Mint a DOI (or ARK/Handle) for the released dataset version and use a dataset-scoped URI for id, distinct from the project landing page.

description: Maintainer email domain is recorded as 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' ('havard'), and one external resource, 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus', is given without a URI scheme. The record flags the first as transcribed verbatim from the source and does not adjudicate it.
recommendation: Verify the maintainer address with the institution and normalize external resource entries to absolute https URLs.

description: license_and_use_terms conflates two distinct objects: the MIT License applies to the chorus-ai code, while no license is named for the data. The access terms recorded are those of one route (the AIM-AHEAD training program registration), not a general data use agreement, so reuse permissions for the dataset itself remain unstated.
recommendation: Name the data use agreement governing dataset access and its reuse and redistribution permissions, kept separate from the software license.

description: No regulatory determination is recorded for a US multicenter clinical dataset: regulatory_restrictions carries confidentiality_level 'restricted' and access-control statements but no HIPAA status, no other_compliance entries, and no governance committee contact of record (contacts appear only as individual emails under maintainers and data_governance.access_review_process).
recommendation: Record the HIPAA compliance determination (limited data set, de-identified, or covered) and designate a governance committee contact for the dataset.

description: No version identity or version tracking: version, version_access and errata are all absent, and updates.source_caveats states that no release cadence or versioning policy is reported. The dataset is described as 'partially released' and actively growing (50,000 toward 100,000 admissions), so results computed on it cannot be pinned to a citable state.
recommendation: Assign version numbers to released snapshots, document how prior versions are accessed inside the enclave, and state the expected release cadence.

description: No variable-level metadata anywhere: variables and is_tabular are absent, despite 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized tabular EHR data being the largest component of the release. Conformance to the OMOP CDM partially substitutes by reference but does not document CHoRUS-specific extensions (the nursing flowsheet schema is described as 'OMOP schema with extensions').
recommendation: Publish a data dictionary for the delivered OMOP tables, flagging CHoRUS extensions to the standard vocabulary and flowsheet schema.

description: No bias documentation: known_biases and future_use_impacts are absent, and no demographic composition is reported for the cohort (subpopulations distinguish ICU/PICU/NICU only). The record's own representativeness_limitation concedes that the achieved demographic, geographic and clinical distribution is unreported, which is a substantive gap for a dataset whose stated purpose is equitable AI.
recommendation: Report cohort demographics per contributing site and categorize known representational biases using the BiasTypeEnum taxonomy, with anticipated downstream social impacts and mitigations.

description: Cross-platform integration is thin: publisher, citation, doi and related_datasets are all absent. Sibling Bridge2AI data generation projects are referenced in prose but no typed dataset relationship is recorded, and there is no recommended citation for a dataset whose funder mandates attribution.
recommendation: Declare the publishing platform of record, add a recommended citation with DOI, and link sibling Bridge2AI datasets with typed relationships.

description: Several capabilities are documented in fields that ordinarily describe realized dataset properties but are stated in the future tense: splits (a holdout test set the award abstract says will be provisioned) and labeling_strategies (an annotation environment that 'will label data'). Each carries an explicit source_caveat, so the record is not misleading, but a consumer parsing the fields without the caveats would over-read the release.
recommendation: Keep planned capabilities in a roadmap field or prefix them in-field, reserving splits and labeling_strategies for realized artifacts.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true and the cohort includes pediatric and neonatal ICU admissions, but there is no informed_consent block at all: no consent procedure, no waiver of consent, no HIPAA authorization statement, and no parental permission/assent discussion. direct_collection.is_direct=false explains that data were not collected from individuals for this purpose, which is relevant context but is not consent documentation.
recommendation: Add informed_consent recording the regulatory basis for retrospective use (e.g. IRB waiver of consent under 45 CFR 46.116, HIPAA waiver of authorization under 45 CFR 164.512(i)), or state explicitly that the bundle does not document one.

description: involves_human_subjects=true but no institutional review board, ethics committee, or reviewing organization is named. ethical_reviews documents community-facing ethics focus groups (a project workstream) rather than oversight of the data collection, and its own source_caveats states that no IRB, ethics committee or compliance certification is named. data_protection_impacts is absent entirely.
recommendation: Add the reviewing IRB(s) and protocol/approval identifiers for the contributing sites, and a data protection impact assessment for the enclave, or state that the source bundle contains none.

description: The dataset is PHI-derived clinical data from 14 US hospitals, yet no regulatory framework is asserted: regulatory_restrictions, confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are all absent. Confidentiality is conveyed only in prose ('Every data type is listed with controlled access') and through data_governance.
recommendation: Add regulatory_restrictions with hipaa_compliant status and a confidentiality_level enum value so that compliance posture is machine-readable rather than inferable from prose.

description: No persistent identifier exists. doi is absent, no RRID is present, and id is https://chorus4ai.org/ — byte-identical to the page value and resolving to the project homepage rather than to this dataset. The record itself notes the site carries a banner warning of potential modification, which weakens any persistence claim for that URL.
recommendation: Mint a DOI (or ARK/Handle) for the released dataset and record it in doi, reserving id for a dataset-specific URI distinct from the landing page.

description: status is 'released' and distribution_dates reports a dataset available to approved users as of August 2025, but version, version_access, errata, citation, doi and publisher are all absent. A released, citable dataset with no version string and no citation cannot be referenced reproducibly in a publication.
recommendation: Assign a version to the August 2025 release, add citation and publisher, and document how prior versions remain reachable.

description: The dataset's dominant component is 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized tabular EHR data, yet variables is absent, is_tabular is absent, and no data dictionary is provided. subsets name content categories (demographics, medications, procedures, flowsheets, diagnoses) but carry no variable-level metadata or identifiers.
recommendation: Add variable-level metadata (or an explicit pointer to the OMOP CDM table/field specification actually instantiated, with any site-specific extensions) and set is_tabular.

description: No data quality documentation: anomalies and missing_data_documentation are both absent. For retrospective EHR and high-frequency flowsheet/waveform data, missingness and device artifact are the dominant quality concerns. cleaning_strategies states that characterization reports are returned to contributing sites, so quality findings evidently exist but none are reported to users.
recommendation: Summarize characterization-report findings as anomalies, and document per-modality missingness patterns and their handling.

description: participant_privacy.reidentification_risk is populated but contains no assessment: 'The project describes transforming data using approaches that limit re-identification, and patient-focused efforts to determine ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy' restates mitigation rather than characterizing residual risk. No risk level, quantification, or expert determination is offered.
recommendation: State residual re-identification risk explicitly (method of determination, residual risk level, known re-identification vectors such as rare diagnoses, geocoded location, and high-resolution waveform timing).

description: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present=true and the named methods cover clinical notes (OHNLP tokenization) and imaging (de-identification 'in process'), but no method is stated for the largest component, the structured OMOP data, and no standard of record (HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination) is named anywhere. 'transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification' is not a method.
recommendation: Name the deidentification standard applied to structured OMOP data (date shifting, identifier suppression, Safe Harbor/Expert Determination) and the imaging deidentification pipeline (the bundle lists a CTP-deid repository).

description: purposes states a capability to 'acquire, standardize, tokenize, store, visualize and label' data, and tasks/intended_uses centre on supervised model development, but labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses and machine_annotation_tools are all absent. No labels or annotations are described for a dataset advertised as AI-ready.
recommendation: Document whether the released data carry labels or annotations and, if so, how they were produced and quality-assessed.

description: imputation_protocols is absent and no statement is made that imputation was not used, despite EHR-derived content where imputation decisions materially affect downstream models.
recommendation: Add imputation_protocols, including an explicit 'no imputation performed; values are as-recorded' statement if that is the case.

description: No prohibited_uses or discouraged_uses for a controlled-access dataset derived from critically ill patients including minors. intended_uses is rich, but no prohibition on re-identification attempts, redistribution, or clinical deployment of unvalidated models is recorded, and the substantive terms of the signed licensing agreement are not summarized.
recommendation: Add prohibited_uses (re-identification, redistribution, unvalidated clinical deployment) and summarize the key obligations of the licensing agreement.

description: No download_url and no link to any access portal or request form. Access instructions exist only as prose in data_governance.access_review_process (two contact email addresses and a registration form reached through a training program), so a prospective user has no dereferenceable access route.
recommendation: Add a URL for the data access request portal or application form to download_url or a dedicated access field.

description: Released-cohort size is reported inconsistently across sources (website 50,000 admissions vs. webinar 'over 45K unique admissions' as of August 2025), and imaging volume is reported on incommensurable units (7,642 admissions with radiology vs. 1000 images available). The record handles this transparently in source_caveats, instances descriptions and known_limitations rather than silently picking one figure.
recommendation: Retain the caveats; where possible reconcile by reporting both admissions-with-modality and object counts per modality at a stated as-of date.

description: Two malformed locators are carried through faithfully: external_resources lists 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' with no URI scheme, and maintainers records the contact address 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' whose domain is misspelled. The record self-flags the second in source_caveats.
recommendation: Normalize the bare hostname to https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus and annotate the likely intended contact domain while preserving the published string.

description: distribution_formats lists OMOP Common Data Model and OHNLP as 'format' values; these are data standards, not file formats, media types, or delivery packaging. The record itself flags this in per-entry source_caveats, so the mis-typing is disclosed rather than concealed. No media_type or encoding is given for any entry.
recommendation: Separate standard conformance from delivery format, and add media_type and encoding for the actually distributed artifacts.

description: instances carries ontology CURIEs (B2AI_TOPIC:4, :9, :15, :37; B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37, :11, :49) with no human-readable labels, so topic and substrate coverage cannot be understood without resolving an external vocabulary that is not linked.
recommendation: Accompany each CURIE with its label, or link the B2AI topic/substrate vocabulary in external_resources.

description: Software is named only in the prose of preprocessing_strategies, collection_mechanisms and external_resources; no used_software slot is populated anywhere and no tool versions are given, so tooling is discoverable but not machine-readable or version-pinned.
recommendation: Attach used_software entries with names, versions and repository/commit references to the processing steps that produced the released data.

description: The project is titled 'for Equitable AI' and keywords include social determinants of health, but no demographic composition (age, sex, race/ethnicity, payer, geography) is reported for the released cohort, and known_biases contains a single selection_bias entry whose own source_caveats concedes that no measured bias assessment exists.
recommendation: Report demographic distributions per subpopulation and per contributing site, and add a measured representativeness assessment against a reference critical-care population.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true and the dataset comprises hospital records of critically ill patients, but no informed_consent field is present and no waiver of consent is recorded. direct_collection.is_direct=false establishes that collection was retrospective, which is a plausible basis for a consent waiver, but the record never states that a waiver was granted or by whom.
recommendation: Add informed_consent documenting the legal basis for retrospective use at contributing sites (IRB waiver of consent, notice of privacy practices, or broad research consent), naming the approving body where one exists.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true, yet ethical_reviews records only community-facing ethics focus groups and perspective-gathering. No institutional review board, ethics committee, reviewing organization or approval number is named for the dataset, and data_protection_impacts is absent. The record's own source_caveats state this gap explicitly.
recommendation: Add ethical_reviews entries naming the reviewing IRB(s) for the multi-site protocol with approval identifiers, and record a data protection impact assessment for the enclave.

description: is_deidentified describes tokenization and imaging de-identification but names no de-identification standard (HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity), enumerates no identifiers removed, and reports no residual re-identification risk. participant_privacy is populated with protections but carries no reidentification_risk assessment, and data_protection_impacts is absent. For 1.6 billion rows of timestamped ICU EHR data plus waveforms and imaging, the method applied to the structured OMOP data is never stated.
recommendation: State the de-identification standard applied to structured OMOP data, enumerate identifiers removed or shifted (notably admission/event timestamps and ages over 89), and add an explicit residual re-identification risk assessment for the enclave release.

description: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is true and PICU/NICU admissions place minors and neonates in the released data, but no assent procedures, guardian consent procedures, or special protections are documented, and participant_compensation is absent (plausibly not applicable for retrospective data but not stated as such).
recommendation: Document the protections applied to pediatric and neonatal records (guardian permission basis, additional access controls, or restrictions on pediatric subsets) and state explicitly that compensation is not applicable to retrospective collection.

description: No DOI is present for a dataset described as released. The id field is https://chorus4ai.org/, the project homepage, which is byte-identical to the page field. A homepage URL that doubles as the landing page is not a distinct, persistent, dataset-level identifier and will not resolve to a specific release.
recommendation: Mint a DOI (or ARK/Handle) for the released dataset and set id to that persistent identifier, leaving page as the landing page.

description: Two volume disagreements are retained rather than reconciled: the project website reports 50,000 released admissions while the September 2025 webinar reports over 45,000 unique admissions as of August 2025; and the website reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data while the webinar reports roughly 1,000 images available with de-identification in process. The record discloses both disagreements and its ranking rule, which is good provenance practice, but a reuser cannot determine the volume of the release they would receive.
recommendation: Report release-dated counts tied to a version identifier so that admission and imaging volumes are unambiguous for a given release.

description: instances.counts of 1600000000 is disclosed by the record as its own expansion of the rounded website figure '1.6 Billion Rows', not a count reported exactly by any source. The disclosure is appropriate, but the integer reads as more precise than its provenance supports.
recommendation: Either report the rounded figure as text or obtain an exact row count from the enclave at release time.

description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is 'restricted' and the data are US hospital records subject to HIPAA, but no HIPAA, GDPR or export-control determination is recorded. HIPAA and GDPR appear in the record only as topics of a training workshop, which is not a compliance determination for the dataset.
recommendation: Record a hipaa_compliant status and any other applicable frameworks for the released data, distinguishing the determination from training content.

description: The dataset is described as partially released and actively expanding toward 100,000 admissions, but version, version_access and errata are all absent and updates.source_caveats confirms no versioning policy is stated. A user cannot cite, reproduce against, or diff a specific release.
recommendation: Assign a version identifier to the current release, document how prior versions can be accessed inside the enclave, and publish change notes as modalities are added.

description: license_and_use_terms notes an MIT/Apache-2.0 license that the record correctly attributes to the chorus-ai software repositories rather than the clinical dataset, but no data use license is named for a dataset that third_party_sharing.is_shared marks as shared. The licensing agreement is referenced only through the AIM-AHEAD training-program registration flow and is not reproduced.
recommendation: Name and link the data use agreement governing dataset access, distinct from the software licenses.

description: The maintainer contact email 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' contains an apparent misspelling of the domain ('havard'). The record flags it as 'address as printed on the site', so the error is faithfully carried rather than introduced, but the address as recorded is not deliverable.
recommendation: Verify and correct the contact domain, retaining a note if the upstream source is the source of the error.

description: notes reproduces a site-wide banner stating the repository is 'under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' (including the upstream typo 'repoitory'). This is a material availability signal for a prospective reuser, but the record does not state what, if anything, it implies for current access or content.
recommendation: State whether the review affects current access, content or timelines, or note explicitly that the effect is unknown.

description: Temporal ordering is internally contradictory: the dataset is issued 2026-06-17, yet three immunofluorescence archives carry issued: 2026-07-15, a month after the version publication date, and created_on is 2025-02-27, sixteen months before issuance. The record flags the file-date anomaly in source_caveats but supplies no resolution.
recommendation: State explicitly whether the July 2026 immunofluorescence archives were added in a post-publication Dataverse revision, and record that revision in an errata or update entry.

description: Two upstream sources disagree on the release date (CM4AI portal: 'Released on: June 17, 2025'; UVA Dataverse: Publication Date 2026-06-17). The record adopts the Dataverse date and documents the conflict, which is good practice, but the dataset title ('June 2026') and the portal listing remain mutually inconsistent for any user arriving from the portal.
recommendation: Retain the conflict note and additionally record which source was consulted on what date, so downstream users can re-verify.

description: No variable-level metadata at all: variables, is_tabular, is_data_split and is_subpopulation are entirely absent, and the ten ZIP archives carry no per-file content description. A reuser cannot determine what columns, channels or matrices the archives contain without downloading them.
recommendation: Add variables entries (or a data dictionary reference) for the perturb-seq cell atlas matrix and the SEC-MS/AP-MS elution and interaction tables, and set is_tabular where applicable.

description: Distribution format is declared only as the ZIP container (format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip) for all ten archives. ZIP is packaging, not a data format: the record never states whether the contents are mzML, TIFF/OME-TIFF, h5ad, MTX, FASTQ or CSV. This satisfies the distribution question but not the interoperability question.
recommendation: Describe the internal file formats and character encoding of each archive alongside the ZIP container declaration.

description: Reported sample magnitudes cannot be attributed to this release. The portal 'Data Insights' figures (53,788 images, 11,739 genes, 21.4 TB) are read by the record as cumulative project-wide holdings by inference, and the 523-protein figure conflicts with the 464-protein figure on the October 2025 release page. The record correctly declines to assert either for the June 2026 archives, leaving instance counts for this release unstated.
recommendation: Report per-release counts (images, targeted genes, proteins, cells) for the ten archives actually distributed here, or state that they are not published.

description: No software that produced or transformed the distributed archives is named. The Cell Mapping Toolkit / CM4AI integration pipeline is named, but the record states the computed cell maps it produces are explicitly not included in this release; FAIRSCAPE is named for packaging, metadata and provenance-graph production. Neither answers what generated the SEC-MS, AP-MS, immunofluorescence or perturb-seq atlas products that are distributed.
recommendation: Name and version the acquisition and processing software for each modality (e.g. mass-spectrometry search engine, image acquisition/segmentation pipeline, CellRanger or equivalent for the CRISPRi atlas).

description: Preprocessing is documented only as an inference from archive names ('Inferred from the paired archive names ... the June 2026 release listing carries no per-file processing description'), and no cleaning, labeling, annotation-quality or imputation documentation exists. The atlas is known to be a processed product but not how it was processed.
recommendation: Document the CRISPRi atlas processing pipeline (alignment, guide assignment, QC filtering, normalization) and state explicitly whether imputation was used.

description: Governance is partly aspirational relative to the release as distributed: data_governance.notes reports a Data Access Committee as a planned arrangement in the preprint, while all ten archives are listed with public file access; and the commercial-licensing and copyright statements in ip_restrictions are drawn from the preprint and earlier release pages rather than from the June 2026 page, which states only CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
recommendation: Confirm on the current release page whether the dual-licensing and Stanford/UCSF copyright carve-outs still apply to the June 2026 archives.

description: Ethical review contact identity is reconciled across sources with a residual mismatch: Vardit Ravitsky is given affiliation University of Montreal while the contact email domain is thehastingscenter.org. The record discloses the mismatch rather than silently resolving it.
recommendation: Record the affiliation associated with the governance role rather than the authorship affiliation, or note that both are current.

description: No errata and no version-level change log. updates describes only a forward-looking quarterly cadence; the one comparative statement ('adds AP-MS data for treated MDA-MB-468 ... which the October 2025 release did not include') sits in related_datasets.notes and describes a cross-DOI delta, not what changed between Dataverse versions of this DOI. The carried-forward '(2025-06-30)' description stamp and the differing MD5s for same-named October 2025 archives are exactly the kind of item an errata entry should carry.
recommendation: Add an errata list and a per-version change description covering the AP-MS addition, the July 2026 file additions, the checksum changes and the stale description stamp.

description: No downstream social impact analysis (future_use_impacts) and no conflict-of-interest statement, despite a named ethics team and an explicit ethics workstream in the project's stated purposes ('ethical, AI-ready datasets').
recommendation: Record the substance of the ethics workstream's review — anticipated downstream impacts of cell-architecture models and mitigations — not only the contacts responsible for it.

description: sampling_strategies[1].is_sample: false is the record's own reading of 'expressed genome-scale' and 'whole-genome', which the record admits no source states in terms. A false flag asserted on inference is weaker evidence than the surrounding prose it rests on.
recommendation: Prefer leaving the boolean unset where the source does not support it, and retain the prose description.

description: The single erratum is self-referential: 'The June 2025 Data Release was published as a revision of the preceding June 2025 release'. The related_datasets chain indicates the June 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, published 2025-07-01) revised the March 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, published 2025-03-03), so the antecedent release name appears to be wrong.
recommendation: Correct the erratum text to name the March 2025 release as the revised predecessor, or state explicitly which pair of releases the erratum describes.

description: Version numbering is non-monotonic across the release chain: the top-level version for this June 2026 release is '2.0', while version_access records the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases as version 2.1. A successor release carrying a lower version string than its predecessors is implausible and will confuse automated version ordering.
recommendation: Reconcile the version string with the Dataverse version history, or add a note distinguishing the Dataverse draft/major version label ('V2') from the semantic release version.

description: No software is named that produced or transformed the data actually distributed in this release. The named tooling is either capture instrumentation (10x Genomics 3'HT kit, pipetting robot, confocal microscopy), metadata/packaging production (FAIRSCAPE), hosting and sharing (NDEx, MassIVE, Figshare), or a pipeline the record itself states produced outputs not present here (MuSIC / Cell Mapping Toolkit, IMP, node2vec, the HPA deep-learning image model). A reuser cannot determine what software generated the ten archives.
recommendation: Name, with versions, the acquisition-to-archive software that produced the released files (e.g. mass-spectrometry search/quantification software for the AP-MS and SEC-MS packages, the CellRanger or equivalent pipeline for perturb-seq, and the imaging export/conversion software), using used_software on the relevant processing strategies.

description: Every distributed file is described only as a ZIP container (format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip); no internal data format (e.g. mzML, mzTab, TIFF/OME-TIFF, h5ad, MTX, FASTQ/SRA) and no character encoding is documented for any archive.
recommendation: Document the internal file formats and encodings of each archive, so a reuser can tell what to parse before a multi-gigabyte download.

description: No variable-level metadata is provided anywhere in the record: the variables slot is absent entirely, so the columns, channels and measured fields inside the mass-spectrometry, perturb-seq and image archives are undocumented.
recommendation: Add variable metadata (or a pointer to a per-modality data dictionary inside the RO-Crate) with identifiers and descriptions for the tabular outputs in each archive.

description: No data anomalies, sampling strategies, or missing-data documentation are recorded. The anomalies, sampling_strategies and missing_data_documentation slots are all absent; the extensive source_caveats concern disagreements between metadata sources, not quality issues in the data themselves.
recommendation: Document known data-level quality issues (failed replicates, low-confidence identifications, out-of-focus fields, dropout in single-cell libraries) and how missing values are represented.

description: No processing of the released data is documented: preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are all absent, and notes explicitly scope the MuSIC pipeline description to tooling and future releases rather than to these files.
recommendation: Describe the processing each modality's released archive underwent between instrument output and deposit, even where that processing is minimal, and state explicitly where no processing was applied.

description: Instance-level counts are not reported for this release: the instances entries carry no counts of images, cells, proteins or interactions, and the record's own source_caveats note that the June 2026 listing states no protein count. Quantification is available only at file level (10 files, 12,601,718,300 bytes).
recommendation: Report per-modality instance counts (images per condition, cells per perturb-seq library, proteins assayed) for this release once the source listing supports them.

description: The stated maintenance horizon and the recorded funding period do not align: updates.update_details promises quarterly updates 'through the end of the project in November 2026', while the funders notes give the NIH project period as 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31.
recommendation: State whether the project end date reflects a no-cost extension or a separate supplement period, or align the two dates.

description: No download_url slot is populated. Access is recoverable only from distribution_formats.access_urls, page and publisher, all of which carry the same Dataverse landing-page URL; no per-file retrieval endpoint or Data Access API base URL is given despite the API being mentioned in prose.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the Dataverse Data Access API endpoint and, where possible, per-file access URLs keyed to the recorded file identifiers.

description: No future_use_impacts (rai:dataSocialImpact) analysis and no conflict-of-interest statement accompany the ethical review, so anticipated downstream social impacts of the released maps and their mitigations are undocumented.
recommendation: Add a future_use_impacts entry covering anticipated downstream social impacts of AI models trained on these data and the mitigations the Ethics module envisages.

description: Only one bias is categorized (representation_bias, cell lines not representing population variation). Plausible biases specific to the modalities — antibody-availability bias in the immunofluorescence protein panel, detectability bias in SEC-MS/AP-MS toward abundant and soluble complexes, guide-library coverage bias in the CRISPRi screen — are not categorized.
recommendation: Add typed bias entries for antibody/panel selection, mass-spectrometry detectability, and CRISPR library coverage.

description: The two ethical_reviews entries carry byte-identical review_details prose, differing only in contact_person, and describe an oversight role rather than a completed review with a date, determination or reference. data_protection_impacts is absent.
recommendation: Record the determination itself (who reviewed what, when, and with what outcome) rather than restating the oversight remit once per contact.

description: Seven of the ten file collections are typed collection_type: processed_data, but no preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools or imputation_protocols are present. A reader cannot tell how raw AP-MS, SEC-MS or perturb-seq output became the distributed processed archives.
recommendation: Add preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies entries describing the per-modality pipelines (spectral search and quantification for MS, alignment and guide assignment for perturb-seq, image QC for IF) that produced the archives marked processed_data.

description: No software is named as having produced or transformed the data actually distributed. The tools the record does name fall outside that role: the Cell Mapping Toolkit / MuSIC pipeline is stated by the record itself to produce computed cell maps that 'are not included in this release'; FAIRSCAPE is packaging and provenance-metadata software; NDEx and the UVA Dataverse are sharing and hosting platforms; the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit is acquisition instrumentation.
recommendation: Name the processing software and versions that produced each released archive (for example the MS search/quantification engine, CellRanger or equivalent for the perturb-seq reads, and the image processing toolchain), with repository or DOI links.

description: No variable-level metadata is provided for any subset; the variables slot is entirely absent, so column, channel and measurement semantics inside the ZIP archives are undocumented.
recommendation: Add variables entries (or per-collection data dictionaries) describing at minimum the MS elution-profile table columns, the perturb-seq atlas matrix fields, and the IF image channel-to-target mapping.

description: distribution_formats declares only the container: format ZIP with media_type application/zip. The scientific payload formats inside the archives (image format for the 12.6 GB of IF data, mass-spectrometry table or mzML-family format, perturb-seq matrix format) and character encoding are never stated, which limits interoperability and harmonization.
recommendation: Record the internal file formats and encodings per file collection in addition to the ZIP container, for example OME-TIFF for imaging and TSV/UTF-8 for the elution profile tables.

description: No instance or sample counts are reported at release level: instances lists four instance types with no counts, and source_caveats explicitly declines to assert the project-level totals (1,374 interactions, 53,788 images, 11,739 genes) as release totals. total_file_count: 10 counts archives, not samples.
recommendation: State per-modality counts for this release (images, proteins/baits, guides and cells, elution fractions), even as approximate figures derived from the deposited archives.

description: No change log or errata for this release: errata is absent and updates carries only a forward-looking cadence ('quarterly ... through the end of the project in November 2026'). What changed relative to the October 2025 release can only be inferred from related_datasets notes.
recommendation: Add an errata or release-notes entry stating the delta for V2.0 (notably the addition of AP-MS data for paclitaxel- and vorinostat-treated MDA-MB-468 and the July 15 2026 addition of the three IF image archives).

description: No data anomalies, outliers, batch effects or missing-data documentation are recorded: anomalies and missing_data_documentation are both absent, even though the release spans four assay modalities with partially overlapping protein coverage.
recommendation: Document known quality issues per modality (failed baits, low-confidence guides, out-of-focus or discarded images) and how missingness across the incompletely overlapping protein sets should be handled.

description: The only access URL given is a truncated Dataverse API root, https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/, with no datafile identifier appended, so it does not resolve to any downloadable object; the dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the DOI-resolved dataset landing page and give per-collection access URLs including the datafile identifiers.

description: The conforms_to RO-Crate claim is, by the record's own admission, carried from the tier-3 preprint and the March/June 2025 releases: 'the June 2026 release page does not itself restate the packaging format, and its file listing names only cm4ai_release_metadata.zip without stating its internal format.' The conformance assertion is therefore unverified for the version being described.
recommendation: Confirm and state the packaging format of cm4ai_release_metadata.zip for V2.0, or scope the RO-Crate claim to the releases in which it was asserted.

description: Inherited date anomalies are disclosed but unresolved: the release page's Dataset Description block is dated 2025-06-30 on a release published 2026-06-17, and created_on 2025-02-27 is 'reused verbatim from earlier releases'. Top-level ordering (created_on 2025-02-27 < issued 2026-06-17 < last_updated_on 2026-07-15) is itself consistent.
recommendation: Correct or annotate the creation date so it reflects this release's data generation window rather than the collection's first deposit.

description: The KOLF2.1J line is described as 'derived from a healthy male Northern European donor' available via HipSci, i.e. donor-derived human material, while human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false. The determination is defensible for an established, distributed line, but the consent and ethical provenance of the originating donation are not referenced.
recommendation: Cite the HipSci/ATCC consent and ethical-sourcing provenance for the originating cell lines to close the chain of custody, without changing the human-subjects determination.

description: Regulatory metadata is thin on the classification axis: confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are unpopulated; regulatory_restrictions records only 'FDA Regulated: No; no export control or regulatory restriction is stated'. Anticipated downstream social impacts (future_use_impacts) are likewise absent despite a substantial ethics programme.
recommendation: Add an explicit confidentiality classification (public/open for this CC BY-NC-SA release) and a future_use_impacts entry capturing the Ethics Module's anticipated social impacts of AI-ready cell maps.

description: version_access.latest_version_doi is doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42, an identifier that appears nowhere else in the record and that conflicts with the record's own DOI for the latest listed version (3.1.0 = doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66, listed in versions_available and in doi/id/citation).
recommendation: Correct latest_version_doi to 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, or state explicitly which release 10.13026/37yb-1t42 designates if a newer version exists.

description: Unreconciled HIPAA characterization: regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant is 'compliant' and other_compliance states HIPAA de-identification rules were applied, while regulatory_restrictions.source_caveats records that the Data Transfer and Use Agreement calls the transferred data personally identifiable information 'not covered under HIPAA, FERPA, or similar laws'. The record flags the conflict but leaves a downstream user unable to determine the operative regime for the raw-audio transfer.
recommendation: State which regime governs which tier (registered-access features vs controlled-access raw audio) rather than recording both characterizations side by side.

description: keywords contains only four generic terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). No method terms (spectrogram, MFCC, articulatory features, speech), no condition terms (Parkinson's disease, dysphonia, depression, COPD) and no modality terms, although all of these are described at length elsewhere in the record.
recommendation: Expand keywords to at least 8-12 terms covering domain, modality, methods and represented conditions so that the record is discoverable by condition and by feature type.

description: data_protection_impacts states that no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted, for a dataset that the record itself classifies as containing race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic, mental-health and clinical-diagnosis data derived from a biometric signal. The absence is honestly reported, but it is a substantive governance gap rather than a documentation gap.

description: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false while the same block states that 'K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved' and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states that voice cannot be fully de-identified. The claims are reconcilable for this release (raw audio is withheld and direct identifiers removed), but the boolean reads more absolutely than the surrounding prose.
recommendation: Qualify the boolean in deidentification_details to distinguish direct identifiers (removed) from quasi-identifier combinations (not k-anonymized).

description: The participant count of 833 is attributed to version 3.1.0 in description and instances.counts, while source_caveats records that the figure comes from documentation written against version 3.0, and related_datasets notes that 3.0.0 itself added 391 participants over 2.0.1. The record discloses the provenance of the figure but still asserts it for 3.1.0.

description: No data-standard conformance is asserted for this release: conforms_to is absent and conforms_to_schema names the metadata record's own schema (w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema) rather than a standard the data conforms to. source_caveats explains that earlier releases were converted to BIDS v1.9.0 but that the 3.1.0 features/metadata/phenotype layout states no such conformance.

description: Several schema slots that the rubric reads are unused even though equivalent content exists elsewhere: download_url (access URLs appear only inside distribution_formats and data_governance.access_review_process), is_tabular, character encoding on any distributed file, Parquet media_type, imputation_protocols, and data_governance.committee_contact (the DACO mailbox appears only in notes).

description: maintainers records NIH under role 'government_agency' with maintainer_details describing award support. That is funding provenance rather than maintenance of the released artifact, and it duplicates funders.

description: variables enumerates only four fields (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames) for a release whose phenotype directory holds dozens of diagnosis and questionnaire tables. Column-level semantics are delegated to the per-file JSON data dictionaries, which are described but not enumerated in the record.

description: updates.frequency states a semi-annual (twice yearly) cadence, but the release history the record itself supplies is denser and irregular: 2025-01-17 (1.1), 2025-04-16 (2.0.0), 2025-08-18 (2.0.1), 2025-12-16 (3.0.0), 2026-05-01 (3.1.0) — five releases in roughly sixteen months. The record caveats that the cadence statement was written against Health Data Nexus hosting, but does not reconcile it with the observed PhysioNet release pattern.

description: version_access.latest_version_doi is given as doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42, which related_datasets (relationship_type: is_version_of) identifies as the concept DOI resolving to the latest version. The DOI of the version actually described by this record is 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. recommendation: Either record the resolved version DOI (10.13026/8xbn-nq66) in latest_version_doi, or rename/annotate the value explicitly as the concept DOI.

description: keywords contains only four broad terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). No clinical condition (Parkinson's disease, ALS, laryngeal cancer, depression), no modality or method term (spectrogram, MFCC, acoustic features, speech), and no data-type term appears, despite all of these being prominent in the description and phenotype inventory. description: The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated. Platform access is nonetheless locatable: distribution_formats.access_urls give https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ for both formats, raw_sources.access_url gives the Synapse controlled-access location, and license_and_use_terms states the credentialing steps.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the PhysioNet content URL so machine consumers do not have to reach into distribution_formats.

description: content_warnings.content_warnings_present is false while a warnings entry is supplied. The record explains the pairing (the warning describes free-speech transcripts removed at 1.1 and excluded from the feature-only 3.0.0/3.1.0 releases), so the semantics are recoverable, but the boolean and the populated list read as contradictory to a consumer that reads only the flag.

description: sensitive_elements carries an acknowledged internal conflict: the healthsheet inventory lists race, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health information as present, while the version 3.0.0 de-identification account states that all REDCap-flagged sensitive fields and highly sensitive non-identifying elements (household income, mental health status, traumatic life experiences) were removed. description: variables enumerates only four elements (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames) for a release whose phenotype directory holds dozens of tables across confounders, demographics, eighteen diagnosis tables, enrollment and thirteen questionnaires. The record compensates by documenting that every table ships a companion JSON data dictionary carrying description, question text and data type.

description: conforms_to is deliberately omitted, with source_caveats explaining that the BIDS 1.9.0 conversion describes the audio dataset's folder layout rather than this feature-only release. The omission is honest, but it leaves no data-level community-standard conformance assertion for the released artifact; ICD-10 appears only as a labeling protocol and conforms_to_schema describes the datasheet, not the data.
recommendation: State any standard the released tables do follow (for example the phenotype/JSON data-dictionary convention, ICD-10 coding of diagnosis columns) in conforms_to, scoped to this release.

description: The RRID carried in the citation string (RRID:SCR_007345) is the resource identifier of PhysioNet, the hosting platform, not of the Bridge2AI-Voice dataset. The format is valid and the usage follows PhysioNet's own citation convention, but the identifier does not uniquely identify this dataset.
recommendation: Keep the platform RRID in the citation but note that dataset-level identification rests on the version DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66.

description: collection_timeframes supplies no start or end dates. The twelve-month figure is caveated as drawn from documentation written against versions 2.0.0/3.0.0, and the record itself observes that the cohort accumulated across releases from 306 to 833 participants, so the stated span probably does not describe the assembly of the released cohort.
recommendation: Record first and last collection dates for the 3.1.0 cohort, or state that they are unavailable from any source.

description: Only four keywords are supplied (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice), below the five-keyword threshold, and all four are generic. None names a disease cohort (Parkinson's, ALS, dysphonia, COPD, depression), a modality term (speech, cough, breath, spectrogram, MFCC), a method term (machine learning, acoustic features, audiomics) or the hosting platform. A dataset spanning four clinical cohorts is under-indexed for discovery by exactly the terms a searcher would use.
recommendation: Expand keywords to at least 8-12 terms covering the four disorder cohorts, the acoustic modalities and feature families, audiomics, and PhysioNet.

description: No data_protection_impacts entry is present although the release carries health, mental-health, race, ethnicity and sexual-orientation derived data and the record itself assesses residual re-identification risk. The absence is disclosed rather than silent: source_caveats states 'the project documentation states that no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted'. The disclosure is good practice, but the DPIA limb of Element 4 sub-element 1 remains substantively unmet.
recommendation: Conduct and record a data protection impact assessment covering the derived-feature release, given the acknowledged inherent identifiability of voice-derived signals.

description: conforms_to is deliberately not asserted for this release, so no community data standard is claimed for the distributed features and phenotype tables. source_caveats explains that BIDS 1.9.0 conformance belongs to the controlled-access raw audio distribution rather than to the PhysioNet featurized release, and records the BIDS fact against related_datasets instead. conforms_to_schema is populated but points at the datasheet's own metadata schema (w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema), which does not help a consumer harmonize the data.
recommendation: State any content-level standard the featurized release does satisfy, or record an explicit negative conformance statement in conforms_to so the absence is machine-readable rather than confined to prose caveats.

description: The variables list contains four entries (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames) against a release holding hundreds of phenotype columns across 18 diagnosis tables and 13 questionnaire instruments, plus per-feature columns in static_features.tsv. The four documented variables are the cross-file join keys and are documented well, and file_collections states that every table is paired with a JSON data dictionary giving per-column descriptions, question text and data type, so the mechanism for full coverage is disclosed; the datasheet itself nevertheless exposes almost none of it.
recommendation: Either lift a representative subset of phenotype and static-feature variables into variables, or cite the resolvable location of each JSON data dictionary so variable metadata is reachable from the datasheet.

description: No conflict-of-interest statement appears anywhere in the record, although Element 9 sub-element 5 asks for one alongside ethical review. The consortium spans fifteen named lead investigators across twelve institutions and an NIH award, which is the circumstance in which such a statement is normally expected.
recommendation: Add a conflicts-of-interest declaration for the investigator group to the ethical_reviews block.

description: at_risk_populations declines to determine whether the neurological cohort (which includes mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, where capacity to consent may be impaired) or the mood and psychiatric cohort are at-risk groups, recording in source_caveats that 'the bundle makes no statement ... so no determination is recorded here'. The IRB protocol is reported as identifying only children under that heading. Declining to infer beyond the source is methodologically correct for the datasheet, but it leaves an unresolved protection question for cohorts the dataset demonstrably contains.
recommendation: Obtain and record the protocol's position on capacity assessment and surrogate or assented consent for the cognitive-impairment cohort.

description: Three declared schema slots that the rubric names as evidence paths are unpopulated, with the substance carried elsewhere: download_url is empty (access URLs appear under distribution_formats.access_urls and data_governance.access_review_process); is_tabular is absent although the phenotype and static-feature tables are plainly tabular; character encoding is not stated for any distributed file.
recommendation: Populate download_url, set is_tabular, and declare the character encoding of the tab-delimited tables and JSON dictionaries.

description: Ontology references are given as bare CURIEs without labels or resolvable prefixes: instances carry data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:36 and data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:69. A reader cannot determine what topic or substrate is meant from the datasheet alone, even though the same concepts are described richly in prose elsewhere in the record.
recommendation: Accompany each CURIE with its human-readable label and register the B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE prefixes against a resolvable namespace.

description: Several genuine source conflicts exist but are surfaced and adjudicated rather than concealed, which is the correct handling and is recorded here as a positive consistency finding rather than a defect: award identifiers differ across sources (PhysioNet 3OT2OD032720-01S1, RePORTER 3OT2OD032720-01S3, publication 1OT2OD032720-01, and a garbled documentation footer), with the stable core project number OT2OD032720 identified; the healthsheet answer 'No, they are unrelated' on instance relationships is recorded beside the release notes describing repeated sessions per participant; and the ~61,937 recording figure for version 3.0 is set beside the 28,640-32,522 per-feature counts for 3.1.0 with no false reconciliation attempted.
recommendation: No change required; retain this caveat discipline in future releases.

description: Subpopulation characterization is qualitative only. subpopulations.identification names the dimensions collected (age, gender, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic status) and distribution describes the skew and its causes, but no counts or percentages are given for any demographic stratum, nor per-cohort participant counts against the 833 total. A user assessing fitness for a fairness study cannot size any subgroup from the datasheet.
recommendation: Add per-cohort and per-demographic-stratum counts, which the phenotype demographics tables already support.

description: version_access.latest_version_doi is doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42, which differs from this record's doi of 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. This is not an error: version_details explains that 10.13026/37yb-1t42 is the resolver DOI for the latest version while 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 pins version 3.1.0. The field name alone could nonetheless be read as contradicting the record's own identifier.
recommendation: Rename or annotate the slot to make clear it holds a concept-level resolver DOI rather than the DOI of the version described.

description: sensitive_elements_present=false and confidential_elements_present=false are asserted for a release comprising retinal imaging (DICOM), continuous glucose traces, wrist-worn biometric signals (heart rate, SpO2, sleep, stress) and in-home environmental sensing. These declarations contradict the same record's restricted confidentiality_level, its verified-ID plus license-assent access gate, its static watermarking of released copies, and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, which concedes a theoretical future re-identification risk from AI inference. A dataset that needs watermarking and a DUA to protect subjects is not plausibly free of sensitive elements, even post-Safe-Harbor.
recommendation: Set sensitive_elements_present=true with a sensitivity_details entry distinguishing 'contains no direct HIPAA identifiers' from 'contains sensitive health and biometric modalities'. The healthsheet's 'No' answer concerns offensive or distressing content and should not be carried into the sensitivity flag.

description: Institutional attribution is internally divergent in the structured fields, not only in prose. creators.affiliations[0] and data_governance.accountable_organization both assert Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) as the accountable organization and PI affiliation, while ethical_reviews.reviewing_organization and human_subject_research.ethics_review_board assert the University of Washington IRB with a UW Human Subjects Division address, and NIH RePORTER is reported as recording award OT2OD032644 to the University of Washington. A consumer reading only the machine-readable fields obtains an institutional attribution that the record's own source_caveats says is contested.
